title.en: Quarter-turn ball valve with bore and seat cutaway

summary: Make a two-port ball-valve cutaway show how the handle, stem, bored ball and seat interfaces correspond at its end positions.
objective: Make a two-port ball-valve cutaway show how the handle, stem, bored ball and seat interfaces correspond at its end positions.
intent_signals: Make a two-port ball-valve cutaway show how the handle, stem, bored ball and seat interfaces correspond at its end positions.
example_prompts: Build an explorable quarter-turn ball valve with bore and seat cutaway and expose its construction at close range.

principles: Use a two-port on/off teaching model. Distinguish the solid pressure-boundary shell, internal passage, ball bore, seats and stem penetration; a sphere pasted between pipes does not describe the mechanism.
The referenced SK product is intended for fully open or fully closed operation. Intermediate angles here expose the geometry during transition, not a recommended throttling regime.
implementation: Construct a finite-thickness body around two coaxial port passages. Put a bored ball between two annular seats, with a stem axis perpendicular to the port axis and a handle attached to that stem. Give the stem seal and seat regions separate selectable groups; decorative threads must not fill the passage.

Set theta in[0,pi/2] as the authoritative actuation angle: zero aligns the ball bore with the two ports; pi/2 turns the bore across them. Derive ball, stem and handle transforms from theta. Keep cutaway planes and exploded offsets as separate inspection state.

At the closed endpoint inspect the seat/ball interface around the port: the authored bore must not leave a through-opening there. Show open/closed labels from theta and a separate transitioning label between endpoints; do not derive flow rate from cos(theta), color or exposed area.

Retain body wall, ball-bore rim, annular seats and handle offset in a hero closeup. In an overview omit thread helices and small packing hardware before removing the major seal boundaries. A translucent body is a view choice, not glass construction.

Offer select-seat, rotate-to-endpoint, reveal-passage and reset actions. If direction arrows are shown at open, label them a chosen illustrative direction; the cited SK design permits bidirectional flow.
observable_checks: At zero, a section through the port axis shows a connected open passage; at pi/2 the bore no longer connects the two seat openings in the assembled geometry.
Rotate repeatedly and reset: the handle remains keyed to the stem and ball; cutaway visibility changes neither theta nor the operational label.
Inspect wall thickness and seat boundaries under neutral shading so highlights cannot conceal accidental holes or intersecting components.

known_limits: No seal deformation, torque, pressure drop, leakage, pressure rating or fluid simulation. Product-specific spring and packing details are not certified by this simplified layout.
Authored construction and prospective checks; no runtime artifact, render or material test has been executed for this record.
creative_affordances: Use an industrial cutaway, oversized classroom prop or stylized utility valve. Keep an open/closed end-state distinction without copying branding.

claims.statement: Swagelok documents quarter-turn operation, a directional handle, a floating ball and seats for its SK series; it states its ball valves are designed for fully open or fully closed use.
claims.scope: Named manufacturer construction and use scope; no transferred product ratings or universal throttling claim.
